mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.0% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% indicates labor market tightness that accelerates consumer spending and corporate profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand that increases corporate revenue visibility, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to generate positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.04 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 100.0 during post-shock recovery periods indicates manufacturing sector stabilization that precedes improved corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO > 100.0 during post-shock recovery, or Rank IC falls below 0.04 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth in the most recent quarter signals sustained economic expansion that increases corporate earnings visibility, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with positive GDPC1 growth, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 1.0% signals monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, or Rank IC is below -0.04 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) signals labor market strength that boosts consumer confidence and corporate margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC is below 0.04 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a federal funds rate above 1.0% compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.0% during tightening cycles, or Rank IC falls below -0.03 over 2-year rolling windows.
